classification.difficultyReason: Interpret bisection to obtain both half-chord lengths, then substitute them into the intersecting chord product rule and solve for the other segment.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.sourceRegion: Bottom row, left column, part fff
spec.description: Circle with horizontal chord AB and sloping chord DC intersecting at P. PC is labelled x. Preserve the absence of a centre, right-angle mark and bisection ticks. Source decorative colours are replaced by ordinary black geometry.
spec.mathematics: P bisects AB, so AP = PB = 20 cm. Intersecting chords satisfy AP × PB = CP × PD. Diagram proportions are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only x and point names appear in the question diagram; numerical results belong in answer fields.

answer.worked:
Since $CD$ bisects $AB$,
$$\begin{aligned}AP = PB &= \frac{40}{2}\\&=20\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}$$
The products of the intercepts of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}AP\times PB &= CP\times PD\\20\times20 &= 25x\\400 &= 25x\\x &= 16\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}$$
